_comment: Blocks of languages/whence/SPEC.md that specstale.py's T001 rule reports and a round has HAND-READ and found NOT stale. Round 507 (skills B) created this file with all 7 of its first run's surviving findings, after auditing 11 blocks and correcting the 4 that were genuinely stale in SPEC.md itself (1592, 4551, 4584, 4948 at the pre-fix line numbers) rather than listing them here. An entry is a CLAIM, not a mute: keys are content pins (version + digest of the bullet's first line, never a file:line -- round 462 measured that a SPEC line number is not durable), so an entry EXPIRES the moment its bullet is rewritten, and specstale reports every expired entry as T003. Add an entry ONLY after reading the bullet and the code it describes, and say in `reason` what you checked. Round 507 removed one entry the same round it wrote it: fixing the sentence splitter (a `.py` claim's paragraph was leaking its neighbours' identifiers, because a sentence OPENING with a version never split) deleted the `_type_spec_expr` overlap that entry excused, and T003 said so on the next run. That is the control working on a real change rather than a synthetic one.
